scenario: AITA for being upset with my wife for suggesting we go to a party only a couple of months after our daughter's death? | I'll French, so pardon my English. AITA here?

prediction.raw: I'm so sorry to hear about your loss. Losing a child is one of the most difficult experiences a parent can go through. As for your situation, I would say that you are not the asshole (AITA = 0). It's completely understandable that you would feel upset and resistant to the idea of going to a party so soon after your daughter's passing. Grief is a highly personal and individual experience, and everyone processes it differently. Your wife's suggestion to go to a party may have been well-intentioned, but it's clear that it was not a good idea at this time. You have every right to express your feelings and concerns, and it's not invalidating your wife's feelings to do so. In fact, it's a sign of a healthy relationship that you're able to communicate your emotions and needs with each other. It's also worth noting that your wife's reaction, calling you an asshole, may have been a defensive response to feeling hurt or misunderstood. However, it's not an excuse for using hurtful language, and it's not a productive way to resolve the issue. In this situation, it would be helpful for you and your wife to have a calm and open conversation about your feelings and needs. You could explain to her how you're feeling and why you don't think going to a party is a good idea right now. You could also ask her to consider how you're feeling and why you need some time to grieve. Remember, grief is a journey, and it's okay to take it one step at a time. You and your wife will get through this together, but it's essential to communicate openly and honestly with each other.
